newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel moves on Discount Bank offering.
newsitem.headline: Israel moves on Discount Bank offering.

text.p: Israel's Finance Minister Dan Meridor has asked parliament's Finance Committee to approve a public offering of shares in Israel Discount Bank based on the bank's 1996 financial results, the Treasury said on Sunday.

The offering, which based on Discount's current market valuation will be for about $165 million, was to take place last month. It was delayed after the Securities Authority asked to see more detailed information on the bank's fourth-quarter debt provision.

The offering, now expected to take place in April, will be for 17 percent of equity now held by the government in shares and two series of warrants redeemable three and nine months after the offering.
Shares in Discount, Israel's third-largest bank, already trade on the bourse and the price of the offering will be set close to the time the prospectus is issued.
Twenty-eight percent of the funds raised will come from the shares offered, 32 percent from the warrants redeemable in three months and 40 percent from the nine-month warrants.
The bank's workers will be offered 10 percent of the issue.
Discount, one of several banks taken over by the government after a 1983 bank shares crash, is 79 percent controlled by the state of Israel.
